```{r, include = FALSE}
# A chunk's code sits under "Show code": open when it is what the page is
# about (`fold = "open"`), closed when it only supports it (`fold = "closed"`,
# the default unless the page sets another); `fold = FALSE` shows it plain,
# and so is code of three lines or fewer.
# Its results stay outside, always shown.
.fold_src <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  f <- if (is.null(options$fold)) "closed" else options$fold
  # short code -- three lines or fewer, a chunk or the part of one before
  # its next output -- is shown as it is: folded, it would hide less than
  # the fold itself takes
  if (isFALSE(f) || length(unlist(strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE))) <= 3L) {
    return(.fold_src(x, options))
  }
  paste0("\n\n<details", if (identical(f, "open")) " open", ">",
         "<summary>Show code</summary>\n\n",
         .fold_src(x, options), "\n\n</details>\n\n")
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fold = "open")   # this page: the code is the subject
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment  = "#>"
)
rt_ok <- requireNamespace("rtables", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("formatters", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = rt_ok)
# The pictures of this page's tables: committed in inst/rtf-examples/articles/
# (made by data-raw/gen_article_shots.R, which renders the page with
# RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT set, so .keep() writes the RTF) and copied next to
# the article to be served.
.here <- normalizePath(".")
.keep <- function(x, file) {
  out <- Sys.getenv("RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT")
  if (!nzchar(out)) return(invisible(NULL))
  doc <- if (inherits(x, "rtf_document")) x
         else if (inherits(x, "rtfplot")) rtfreporter::rtf_figures(rtfreporter::rtf_document(), x)
         else rtfreporter::rtf_tables(rtfreporter::rtf_document(), x)
  rtfreporter::generate_rtfreport(doc, file.path(out, file), overwrite = TRUE)
  invisible(NULL)
}
.shot <- function(file) {
  # the package's folder: the one above this page with a DESCRIPTION
  root <- .here
  while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "DESCRIPTION")) && dirname(root) != root) root <- dirname(root)
  src <- file.path(root, "inst", "rtf-examples", "articles", file)
  if (!file.exists(src)) return(invisible(NULL))
  dir.create(file.path(.here, "figures", "articles"), showWarnings = FALSE,
             recursive = TRUE)
  file.copy(src, file.path(.here, "figures", "articles", file), overwrite = TRUE)
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path("figures", "articles", file), error = FALSE)
}
```

```{r setup, eval = TRUE, fold = FALSE}
library(rtfreporter)
```

> **The second path.** This article is about bringing a table you already
> have.  When the statistics are in a cards / cardx ARD, the recommended route
> is a table plan -- see [Get started](rtfreporter.html) and
> [Tables from an ARD](tables-from-ard.html).

An [rtables](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rtables) table --
including the tables [tern](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tern)'s
analysis functions build, which are rtables objects -- goes to RTF through
`as_rtftables()`, as it is.

## From an rtables table to RTF

`as_rtftables()` also accepts any **rtables** `VTableTree` -- including the
tables produced by **tern** analysis functions, which are rtables objects.
They are read through `formatters::matrix_form()`, so nested column splits
become spanning headers, the row-label stub keeps its indentation, and the
titles / footers / referential footnotes flow through.  In-cell footnote
marks `{N}` are rewritten to `^{N}`.

```{r rtables}
library(rtables)

lyt <- basic_table(title = "Table 2", main_footer = "Source: ADSL") |>
  split_cols_by("ARM") |>
  split_rows_by("RACE") |>
  analyze("AGE", afun = function(x) {
    in_rows("Mean (SD)" = rcell(c(mean(x), sd(x)), format = "xx.x (xx.x)"))
  })

set.seed(1)
adsl <- data.frame(
  ARM  = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 30),
  RACE = rep(c("WHITE", "BLACK", "ASIAN"), 20),
  AGE  = rnorm(60, 45, 8)
)
tern_like <- build_table(lyt, adsl)

doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_section(page = 1, header = NULL, footer = NULL) |>
  rtf_tables(as_rtftables(tern_like))

out <- tempfile(fileext = ".rtf")
generate_rtfreport(doc, out, overwrite = TRUE)
file.exists(out)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE}
.keep(doc, "rt_basic.rtf")
.shot("rt_basic.png")
```

The rtables `read` tokens are `"col_header"`, `"alignment"`, `"spanning"`,
`"titles"`, `"footnotes"`, `"indent"`, `"footnote_marks"`; `read = TRUE`
(default) reads them all.

## Splitting a long table across pages

`as_rtftables()` pages the table: `split` and `max_rows` say how, as for any
source -- see [Paginating with as_rtftables()](pagination.html).
